narrative:
The model determined that you have a 30% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and how long you have been employed. The short nine-month duration you asked for actually worked in your favor. Most approved applicants request loans lasting about 19 months, so your shorter term helped pull the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was outweighed by two other important details.

Your checking account is currently in negative balance. Among all approved applicants, only about 13% have a negative balance, while nearly 60% have no checking account at all. This situation pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. Your employment length of four to seven years also pulled the prediction slightly toward approval compared with shorter tenures, but not enough to overcome the negative signal from your checking account.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan. To improve your chances next time, focus on clearing your checking account into positive territory or opening a new account with a healthy balance before reapplying. You may also want to consider requesting a slightly longer loan term if your budget allows, as that pattern is more common among successful applicants.
